title: The Least Popular DnD Opinion: aka "The Problem With Warlocks" – Page 15
snippet: I’ll get right to the point: Warlocks shouldn’t exist in 5e. It’s not that the basic concept is bad (blood pacts and oaths with ancient beings are a staple of the fantasy genre, and they make for fantastic storytelling). No - Warlocks shouldn’t exist, at least not how they are built and played in 5e, because they are fundamentally unfair to the other classes. To begin with, it helps to take a look at the origins of the warlock class. There, the playstyle and build of each class varies - you build up to a concept with the features that you choose, which in turn adapt the method in which you can best play your character. For spellcasters, this is usually in the building of your spell list; for rogues and rangers, it’s in the allocation of skill points; for fighters, it's in feats, which they get broad choice from instead of pre-set class features every time they level up.
